title: Constrained-decoder stress suite for streaming JSON enforcement under backpressure
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Objective: implement an automated, repeatable smoke/stress harness that validates JSON-mode enforcement and constrained-decoder correctness when the serving stack experiences backpressure, KV-cache partial hits, and intermittent tool/function call interleaving. The suite is intended to catch regressions where streaming output becomes nonconformant to a schema due to rate limiting, batching changes, or kernel fallbacks at runtime. This ticket focuses on test scenarios, synthetic workload generation, and acceptance hooks that can be run in CI and as a daily canary job.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Harness can replay 10 canonical prompt families (short, medium, long) with randomized prefix truncation and reproduce deterministic schema failures with a seed.
2) Constrained-decoder must enforce required keys and types for >98% of cases under 95th percentile token latency injection.
3) When a schema violation is detected the run yields a reproducible trace (request id + token stream + kernel selection log) and creates a triage ticket automatically.
4) Daily canary job produces a pass/fail metric visible on the runtime-1.20 stability dashboard and alerts the oncall slack channel on failure.
5) Integration with tool/function mocking: at least 3 interleaving toolcall patterns validated (tool-first, tool-midstream, nested-tool-return).
repro_steps:
1) Checkout branch eng/ENG-341210/stream-harness and run `./scripts/stream-smoke --seed 1234 --prompts canonical-set.json --backpressure 50ms --kv-hitrate 0.6 --tool-interleave-pattern pattern_b`
2) Observe logs under /var/log/redwood/tests/ENG-341210/ for token-by-token outputs and kernel selections.
3) Run `./scripts/collect-trace --request <id>` to gather trace + decoder state.
4) Trigger failing scenario with `--chaos kernel-fallback` to validate fallback handling and schema recovery path.
comments: 2026-03-02 - Design kickoff: aligned with PM on safety threshold (98% schema pass) and agreed to include 3 toolcall patterns. Decided to bias suite toward production token distributions rather than only synthetic ngrams.

2026-03-05 - Engineering sync: Jonah implemented the initial harness and a lightweight mock for tool RPCs. Observed a majority of failures happened when KV-cache hitrate < 0.4 and latency spikes > 80ms.

2026-03-07 - Review feedback from Maria (QA): requested deterministic seeds for all randomized steps and CI artifacts that include both the failing token stream and the decoder state snapshot. Added `--seed` flag and trace collector.

2026-03-09 - PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-runtime/pull/6783 - includes harness and two smoke jobs. Requesting review from runtime and infra. Noted that the kernel selection logs need a small shim to include model-variant tags.

2026-03-11 - Infra run: introduced a canary job on the 1.20 cluster. First run passed, second run failed reproducibly with seed 7421. Root cause traced to a recent batching change that coalesced small tokens and changed decoder tokenization boundaries, causing a required closing bracket to move to a later chunk and be omitted under timeout. Filed follow-up ENG-341998 for batching policy tweak.

2026-03-12 - PM note (Evan): prioritized this for the next runtime-1.20 patch; we should gate the rollout if daily canary fails more than 3 times in 24h. Also asked for customer impact classification in reports.

2026-03-13 - Jonah: added kernel-tagging to logs and a small recovery harness that attempts to request a short re-invocation to finish partial JSONs when streaming detects missing top-level keys. Pushed an interim fix in PR #6795 for quicker mitigation while we investigate batching fallout.
